analysis:
Examined test-only changes. NativeToolStreamRouterTests.swift: base line 419 expected legacy forced mode to throw on " \n"; head lines 418-424 now expect auto mode to stream whitespace as content and forced mode to silently drop ASCII framing whitespace while prose still throws. New test lines 429-469 assert that only space/tab/CR/LF are dropped across legacy, native and MiMo paths at any chunking. They also assert that other Unicode whitespace (VT, FF, NEL, NBSP, ZWSP, LS, IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE, BOM) still raises toolChoiceViolation, and that auto mode preserves the bytes. Lines 472-479 add a scalar-splitting helper.

These tests imply a production change in NativeToolStreamRouter, which is not in this batch. Forced mode now tolerates leading ASCII whitespace before a validated call. That relaxes tool_choice enforcement, which is a response-shaping and correctness concern rather than a confidentiality, attestation or billing control in the threat model (T-007, T-056 concern output correctness, which attestation never proved). Dropping whitespace leaks no plaintext; it withholds bytes rather than emitting them unencrypted, so T-008 is not implicated.

StructuredForcedToolAdmissionTests.swift (added, head lines 1-381) was supplied only as metadata plus a truncated patch excerpt in file_changes. It asserts admitted catalog builds (Qwen3.5, qwen3.6, MiMo, qwen38) for forced tool_choice. It is test-only, but full content was not reviewed.

The integration pass should verify:
- The router implementation drops whitespace only in forced mode.
- The router does not buffer unboundedly while dropping whitespace (availability, T-010/T-029 style).
- The catalog admission list matches production gating code.

No security regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
